title: Lodhi Gardens Delhi – History, Timings & Travel Guide
content:
Lodhi Gardens - Delhi,

Lodhi Gardens in Delhi is a beautiful mix of lush greenery and 15th-century Mughal architecture. Spread over 90 acres, this garden is home to historic tombs, ancient structures, and wide lawns where locals and tourists come to relax, walk, and enjoy the outdoors.

Built during the Lodi dynasty, the park has impressive monuments like Sikandar Lodhi’s Tomb, Muhammad Shah’s Tomb, Sheesh Gumbad, and Bara Gumbad. These structures, surrounded by gardens and pathways, give the place a unique charm where history and nature meet.

Lodhi Gardens is not just about monuments - it’s also one of the best spots in Delhi for morning walks, yoga, birdwatching, or simply enjoying peaceful time away from the city’s rush. Its well-maintained pathways, fountains, and flowering trees make it a favorite for photographers and families.

Best Time to Visit: The gardens are open every day from sunrise to sunset, with free entry for all visitors. Lodi Garden can be visited any time of the year, but the best experience is from October to March, especially in the early morning when the gardens are cool, quiet, and filled with soft light.

How to Reach:

  • By Metro: Nearest station is Jor Bagh (Yellow Line), about a 5-minute walk to the gardens.
  • By Bus/Auto: Well-connected by DTC buses and auto-rickshaws from central and south Delhi.
  • By Car: Parking is available near the entry gates.

Entry Fee: Free for all visitors.

Travel Tip: Pack a light breakfast or snacks - having them under the shade of an ancient dome is one of Delhi’s simplest pleasures.
excerpt: Lodhi Gardens in Delhi is a peaceful green space filled with Mughal-era tombs, domes, and wide lawns. Spread across 90 acres, it’s perfect for morning walks, picnics, and exploring history. With free entry and a calm atmosphere, it’s one of the best places to relax in Delhi.
